events.name: Mario, der Eismann und der Pinguin
events.excerpt: "Splash" - the little penguins jump enthusiastically from the highest icebergs into the cold water. Only Patti, the penguin girl, doesn't dare. One day she builds a boat out of ice and begins a journey south.

events.name: Die Eichhörnchen-Story
events.excerpt: The young squirrel Nico scurries through the park, but doesn't find any nuts on the walnut tree, instead he finds a lot of rubbish. Why isn't the tree bearing nuts? Waltraud Walnussbaum cannot explain this himself.

events.name: Unterscheidet euch!
events.address: Parkaue 29 THEATER AN DER PARKAUE, 10367 Berlin
events.excerpt: People differ from one another. Differences and distinctions between people are a double-edged matter. Some are voluntary and others involuntary; some are visible and others invisible.

events.name: Die fabelhaften Millibillies
events.excerpt: Emilia has dreamed up an entire band: drums, guitar, keyboard, and bass. And suddenly, a boy from her class shows up—Tobi—and he just won’t disappear from her dream!

events.name: Sleeping Beauty
events.address: Oranienburger Straße 32 In den Heckmann Höfen, 10117 Berlin
events.excerpt: A wonderfully beautiful fairy tale about the lovely princess who is fast asleep behind a hedge of thorns. Many princes try to rescue her, but only the prince who arrives at the right moment can break through the hedge of thorns and rescue…

events.name: Aschenputtel - Interactive Theater
events.address: Oranienburger Straße 32 In den Heckmann Höfen, 10117 Berlin
events.excerpt: Interactive theater is a special form of theater in which an experienced actress tells a fairy tale while taking on the various fairy-tale characters and roles.

events.name: Schneewittchen - Mitspieltheater
events.excerpt: Play-along theater is a special form of theater acting in which an experienced actress tells a fairy tale while slipping into the various fairy tale characters and roles.

events.name: aneinander-vorbei
events.excerpt: A musical game about 1,000 wishes and unforgettable moments Theater for the little ones. Two actors and a musician playfully and associatively improvise a story about the exciting encounters between children and adults that happen during a…

events.name: The Spooky Schusch
events.excerpt: On the lonely Dogglspitz mountain live the stubborn deer, the shy chicken, the nasty chamois, the grumpy marmot, and the party-loving rabbit.

events.name: Secret in the house
events.excerpt: It seems to be abandoned. But many things remind of its former inhabitants. Sima and Sophie ask themselves many questions: Who lived here? Who sat at the table in the evening and looked out the window?

events.name: The History of Nutrition
events.excerpt: No more chocolate crises. Candy debates. Cookie conflicts! Parents and caregivers are all too familiar with the discussion about (un)healthy eating.

events.name: Weekend workshops for families
events.excerpt: These one-hour workshops are designed for families who love to play and sing and want to actively prepare for a visit to the children’s opera. Families with children aged six to twelve are welcome to participate.

events.name: Hansel and Gretel: Interactive Theatre | Domäne Dahlem
events.address: Oranienburger Straße 32 In den Heckmann Höfen, 10117 Berlin
events.excerpt: Much to their stepmother’s delight, Hansel and Gretel get lost in the forest. Driven by hunger, they find their way to the witch’s cottage. The witch captures them.

events.name: Guided tour for families
events.excerpt: When was the Komische Oper Berlin founded? What’s the story behind the “komische” name? And what does it actually look like behind the curtain at the Schillertheater?

events.name: Family morning
events.excerpt: During the Berlin Christmas vacations, children and their families have the opportunity to take a look behind the scenes of the Staatsballett Berlin.

events.name: It's the Turtle's Birthday
events.excerpt: It’s the turtle’s birthday. What she’d love most is a head of lettuce—big, green, and juicy. I wonder if anyone will think of that? The lion comes by and gives her a piece of meat; the elephant brings her a bucket of water.

events.name: Hans im Glück
events.excerpt: As a reward for seven years of service, Hans receives a large lump of gold from his master. For Hans, it’s now time to set out into the world, into life, and into freedom.

events.name: Pippi Longstocking
events.venue: Schillertheater - Komische Oper Berlin, Großer Saal
events.excerpt: ‘Ahoy and away!’ Pippi Longstocking is moving into the Villa Villekulla. She plans to wait for her father there, a captain who went missing during their last adventure together on the high seas.

events.name: KLING KLANG
events.excerpt: Does a ‘Klang’ sound or does a ‘Klong’ ring? Does a ‘Dang’ warble or does a ‘Song’ toot? Does a ‘Tut’ sing or does a ‘Träller’ dang? Does a ‘Bing’ bong or does a ‘Kling’ clang?

events.name: Das tapfere Schneiderlein Mitspieltheater I Dahlem
events.excerpt: Interactive theater is a special form of theater in which an experienced actress tells a fairy tale while taking on the various fairy-tale characters and roles.

events.name: Der kleine Muck
events.address: Oranienburger Straße 32 In den Heckmann Höfen, 10117 Berlin
events.excerpt: The shrewd Muck enters the service of a sorceress and discovers a pair of magic slippers that enable him to travel from place to place in the blink of an eye.

events.name: Lotta is moving house
events.excerpt: How on earth can adults be so clueless? Is it really that hard to understand how mean older siblings can be, how you feel after a terrible nightmare, and that woollen jumpers are incredibly itchy?

events.name: No Planet B
events.excerpt: Three young people imagine that a climate catastrophe has struck, and they are sitting in the International Children’s Court.

events.name: The Century of Displacement
events.excerpt: Why do people have to flee or are expelled? What do they experience? The Documentation Centre for Displacement, Expulsion, Reconciliation looks at politically, ethnically and religiously motivated forced migrations in the 20th century in…

events.name: The Bremen Town Musicians - play along theater
events.excerpt: Narrative theater is a special form of theater play in which an experienced actress tells a fairy tale and slips into the various fairy tale characters and roles.

events.name: Laura was here
events.excerpt: The successful production "Laura was here" returns to GRIPS in a new production! A turbulent journey through a Berlin apartment building full of music, humor, and everyday magic, cleverly illuminating togetherness.

events.name: Open printing workshop
events.excerpt: Want to print pictures like a real artist? Kurt Mühlenhaupt created art for children. At the museum, you can create your own art with lots of color, creativity, and fun.

events.name: Johann Ludwig von Fauch
events.excerpt: Palace dragon Johann Ludwig von Fauch leaves his "ancestral palace" - the New Palace in Sanssouci Park - and goes on a journey.

events.name: Try it!
events.excerpt: Are you a violin queen, a keyboard wizard, or more of a guitar hero? Once a month, you can try out different instruments under the guidance of the museum guides.

events.name: Bastel-Buch
events.excerpt: Whether origami, window picture or atmospheric table decoration ... many no longer needed books are too beautiful for the waste paper. We want to give them new life and invite you to a creative craft round!

events.name: Wedding Market
events.excerpt: The Wedding Market takes place on Leopoldplatz every second Sunday of the month from April through November, from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. For the first time, the market will begin as early as April.

events.name: At your service. Castle tales with the chambermaid Sophie
events.excerpt: Who knows the royal court better than she does? Who knows as well as she does who once walked through the magnificent halls and cabinets? And who could tell us more about the people who lived here?

events.name: Die Razzzelbande: What's up Hoverup
events.excerpt: In their songs, the four friends Sharkie, Ahja, Mitch, and Conny recount their everyday adventures at home, as well as those they've experienced while searching for the Golden Tone.

events.name: Jack and the Beanstalk
events.excerpt: Jack and the Beanstalk is a classic fairy tale about a poor boy, Jack, who trades the family cow for magic beans. The beans grow into a giant beanstalk leading to an ogre’s castle in the clouds.

events.name: Dinosaurs! Age of the giant lizards
events.excerpt: Welcome to a world that ruled the earth millions of years ago. Immerse yourself in the fascinating age of dinosaurs and experience the giants of prehistoric times up close.

events.name: In Search of Clues: Design in Berlin
events.excerpt: Join your family* for a tour of the exhibition “Designing for Berlin: Design from the Berlin-Weißensee School of Art”!

events.name: Cheeky like Cupid
events.excerpt: Like an angel but armed with magic arrows, Cupid flies through the castle with many of his fellow creatures. Without any respect, the boisterous horde sits down on royal chairs or watches the castle residents eating or getting dressed.

events.name: Wind energy in the museum park
events.excerpt: You can explore the energy technologies of the past and the future on a stroll through the museum park of the German Museum of Technology.

events.name: Life in the Middle Ages
events.excerpt: On this guided tour through the museum village, you will learn about the culture, agriculture and crafts of the Middle Ages in a hands-on way.

events.name: Family Open Lab – Smart and Sustainable Futures for Agriculture
events.excerpt: What will a farm look like in the future? Perhaps drones will fly over the fields, sensors will measure various soil parameters, and artificial intelligence will assist with the harvest.

events.name: Göttlich!
events.excerpt: Which goddess was a "brainchild"? Who was constantly on the move as the god of travelers and messenger of the gods? What attributes characterize goddesses? You look at marble statues and antique vases and make references to the present.

events.name: Take a Break – and Go Blue!
events.excerpt: Discover the magic of cyanotype printing – a camera-free and completely eco-friendly photographic technique!

events.name: DISCO - Acrobatics * Dinner * Dance
events.excerpt: Let’s Dance! With DISCO – Acrobatics * Dinner * Dance, the Wintergarten Varieté Berlin celebrates the dazzling disco era in all its facets.

events.name: Froggy - the Musical
events.excerpt: The fairy tale "The Frog Prince" is told in a modern, witty, and biting way, without losing the charm of its traditional wisdom. Dr. König, owner of a frog leg factory, gives his daughter Princy a very valuable golden ball pendant.

events.name: Visit to the House of Stars
events.excerpt: What is an observatory, and how does a telescope work? The participating children explore these questions and take a look at one of the world’s longest telescopes together.

events.name: Craft Stories – A Creative Afternoon for Kids
events.excerpt: The Library at the Water Tower warmly invites children ages 3 to 8 to our new, free event series, “Craft Stories”!

events.name: Family Workshop: Printing Workshop
events.excerpt: The exhibition ‘On to New Works! Max Slevogt, Bruno Cassirer and Max Liebermann’ shows the diverse ways in which artists around 1900 experimented with drawing and printmaking for illustrated books.

events.name: Picture Book Cinema. Ida, Ada and Sibylla. Famous female researchers
events.excerpt: Come and listen to a reading of the picture books ‘Ada und die Zahlen-Knack-Maschine’ by Zoë Tucker, ‘Sibylla und der Tulpenraub’ by Benita Roth, and ‘Ida und die Welt hinterm Kaiserzipf’ by Linda Schwalbe.

events.name: Picture book cinema: Poodles, pigs or cats?
events.excerpt: Come and listen to a reading of the picture books ‘Pudel mit Pommes’ by Pija Lindenbaum, ‘Alles Schweine oder was?!’ by Alice Brière-Haquet and Pénélope Paicheler, and ‘Alle sehen eine Katze’ by Brendan Wenzel and Thomas Bodmer.

events.name: Picture Book Cinema: Sitting on the Mat, with Dog, Cat and Rat
events.excerpt: Come and listen to a reading of the picture books ‘Für Hund und Katz ist auch noch Platz’ by Axel Scheffler and Julia Donaldson, ‘Vor meiner Tür auf einer Matte’ by Nadia Budde, and ‘Seht mal her, da sitzt ein Bär’ by Ross Collins.

events.name: Spaceship Earth
events.excerpt: 3, 2, 1 – Lift-off! Climb aboard the planetarium’s spaceship and get ready for an exciting journey through space: after the countdown, everyone takes off and watches from space as our Earth orbits the Sun.

events.name: To Planets by Rocket
events.excerpt: Come along on an exciting, interactive adventure through our solar system!

events.name: The Rainbow Fish and His Friends
events.excerpt: Purple, blue, green, yellow, orange and red: these are the colours of the rainbow, and the rainbow fish shimmers in all these colours too.

events.name: Forum, Flashes of Colour, Fantasy
events.excerpt: Imagine this: right in the heart of the city there is a place where people of all ages come together to dream, reflect and ask questions.

events.name: Product Design & 3D Printing
events.excerpt: Imagine if you could simply make everything you need for everyday life right at home. How would our lives change if we could build things ourselves in the future? And how does that actually work?

events.name: ElternZEITgeschichte
events.excerpt: Guided tours for parents with babies and toddlers through the current temporary exhibition. You are invited to discover together the photography exhibition ‘Skaters & Skateboarders Before and After the Fall of the Wall’, featuring the…

events.name: BODIES THAT SPEAK – Female Artists in Berlin
events.excerpt: 17 female artists. Four generations. One theme: the human body.Following the hugely successful exhibition ‘Faces ofMind’, HAUS. KUNST. MITTE. returns to the human figure as its central visual theme with ‘Bodies that Speak’.

events.name: Little Cosmos Sand
events.excerpt: In this workshop, you’ll be experimenting with kinetic sand, a special material that sticks to itself and can be reshaped over and over again.

events.name: Magic Dream Tree
events.excerpt: The Planetarium Berlin Foundation presents the cult musical "Der Traumzauberbaum" ("The Dream Magic Tree") by Reinhard Lakomy and Monika Ehrhardt-Lakomy in 360-degree fulldome technology with loving visualisations and animations based on…

events.name: Family Backstage Tour
events.excerpt: These guided tours through the auditorium and across the stages, as well as through the rehearsal rooms and the set store at the Deutsche Oper Berlin, offer fascinating insights and interesting facts about the Deutsche Oper Berlin and…

events.name: Afternoon of games for children
events.excerpt: From September onwards, children aged 6 and over are warmly invited to join us for an afternoon of games, accompanied by an adult.

events.name: Scary animal world
events.excerpt: October is known to be the scary month of the year. The animal inhabitants of the zoo also have some almost spooky secrets. Who dares to get to the bottom of the scary myths and stories of the animal kingdom on a tour with a guide?

events.name: Storytime at the Liebermann Villa
events.excerpt: As part of the exhibition ‘On to New Works! Max Slevogt, Bruno Cassirer and Max Liebermann’, the Liebermann Villa on Lake Wannsee invites visitors to listen together and immerse themselves in the world of illustrated fairy tales.

events.name: Open Art Studio for Teens
events.venue: Hamburger Bahnhof - Museum für Gegenwart Berlin
events.excerpt: You’ll be working with what you bring with you: your ideas, your questions, your curiosity. What sort of space is the museum? How much room is there really here for new ideas and experiments?

events.name: Picture-book cinema
events.excerpt: Every Thursday at 4.00 pm, the Kurt Tucholsky Library is showing a picture book cinema in the events room. Come along and see what wonderful stories they have in store for you!

events.name: Pokemon Tausch Samstag
events.excerpt: Whether you’re swapping cards or playing Pokémon Go: have a chat!

events.name: From selfie to emperor: self-portraits
events.excerpt: Act like the Roman emperors! Dream yourself into foreign worlds! Decipher secret messages! Take a look at ancient buildings! Children and their adult companions explore the museums on their own and with a task.

events.name: The mysterious chest and the circus mouse
events.excerpt: Lothar Lusche, a junk dealer, is up to his neck in debt. He is almost broke and to his annoyance, a cheeky, greedy "circus mouse" has taken up residence in his home. Lusche has a lot of trouble catching it.

events.name: DigiQuest
events.excerpt: Quiz rally in the library using the Actionbound app.

events.name: Travelling exhibition: 600 Accordions. Your Stories. Our Berlin – Part 5
events.excerpt: Berlin resident Dieter Plinke has amassed a collection of 600 accordions – a true life's work. They are linked to memories from a wide variety of countries, generations and Berlin neighbourhoods. Through the project "600 Accordions.

events.name: Story Chest
events.excerpt: Every Tuesday at 3 pm, the Wolfdietrich Schnurre Library opens its story box for you!

events.name: Podcasting Studio – MakerSpace
events.excerpt: The podcasting studio offers everything you need to produce your own podcast: with top-of-the-range microphones and headphones, you can create high-quality, professional audio recordings.

events.name: Die drei ??? und die singende Schlange (The three ??? and the singing snake)
events.excerpt: The world's most successful radio play series celebrates its world premiere: "The Three ??? and the Singing Snake" can be experienced for the first time as a 3D radio play in the Zeiss Planetarium.

events.name: Parent-Child Meet-up
events.excerpt: The function room will be turned into a play area. Whilst the children play, parents can chat in a relaxed atmosphere.

events.name: Hänsel und Gretel (Hansel and Gretel) - Varia Vineta
events.excerpt: A poor woodcutter lives at a large forest with his wife and two children. The family has nothing to eat anymore. In great need the parents take the children to the forest.

events.excerpt: Charlie doesn’t want to go to school any more. It’s all Schnapp’s fault – an invisible creature that nobody seems to know about except Charlie.

events.name: Every second Friday: Coding with OSMO
events.excerpt: Discover the exciting world of programming! Learn the basics of programming in a fun way with exciting tools such as Osmo Awbie, Tangram and Words.

events.name: Magical, autumnal, colourful
events.excerpt: Holiday programme at the open-air museum: Off to the autumnal museum village! During the school holidays, there are some brilliant activities on offer for the whole family.

events.name: Crafts with Daniela
events.excerpt: Creative craft fun for young and old alike! Do pop in and join Daniela to make some lovely crafts together in a cosy atmosphere.

events.name: Geisterwelten
events.excerpt: Come to the FEZ if you dare! During the autumn half-term, the FEZ takes on a whole new atmosphere: the large windows are darkened, lights flicker and strange noises echo through the corridors.

events.name: Fall in the Middle Ages
events.excerpt: In the open-air museum, you’ll get a hands-on experience of how people lived, worked and farmed their fields back then.

events.name: Ala Labama's Grand Magic Show
events.venue: Kinder und Familientheater Coq Au Vin (Neukölln)
events.excerpt: The great Ala Labama is coming to your town! Let him whisk you away into his magical world. Sensational tricks await you! Unfortunately, even a great magician can make mistakes, so the highlight of the show—the “rabbit transformation…

events.excerpt: The New Chambers are situated in the heart of Sanssouci Park and were built under Frederick the Great. Large banquet halls and lavishly furnished living and sleeping quarters were intended for the King’s guests.

events.name: Made from plants! Making colors
events.venue: Haus Bastian – Zentrum für Kulturelle Bildung
events.excerpt: What shades of colour can be made from plants? What sort of colours can you find in the paintings at the museum? At Haus Bastian, you’ll explore how colours are made and what they’re made of, and learn how to extract dyes from plants.

events.name: Stars of the Stage: Picture-book cinema, Kamishibai & painting, crafts
events.excerpt: ‘Podesthelden’ is a programme for children aged 3 to 6. Here they can sing, paint, recite rhymes, do crafts and much more! Previously held at the Wasserturm Library.

events.name: Clay Monsters and Plaster Ghosts
events.venue: Haus Bastian – Zentrum für Kulturelle Bildung
events.excerpt: You’ll discover unusual and eerie creatures in the artworks on Museum Island. Do these creatures look familiar to you? Using clay and plaster, and a variety of tools and techniques, you’ll create your own wild or friendly monsters and…

events.name: Kids’ Wednesday
events.excerpt: Come along to Children’s Wednesday at the KW. This creative space is designed for families with children aged 0 to 6 and offers a fun and inspiring environment in which to discover art together.

events.name: Textile printing (Apprentice Weeks)
events.excerpt: Bring along your old clothes and fabric offcuts, and we’ll print new designs on them together.

events.name: DKB Foundation Cultural Workshop
events.excerpt: In October 2026, the DKB Foundation will open a venue dedicated to art, cultural education, social interaction and public dialogue in Berlin’s newly developing Europacity district.

events.name: ANOHA
events.venue: ANOHA Kinderwelt des Jüdischen Museums Berlin
events.excerpt: ANOHA takes the story of Noah from the Torah as its starting point for a journey into the future. At the center of the children's museum is a gigantic ark, 150 different animals - and the children themselves.

events.name: Aquarium Berlin
events.excerpt: The Aquarium Berlin is one of the most famous aquariums in Europe. From colorful reef inhabitants to impressive sharks, from gardening ants to fascinating giant snakes - behind historical facades mysterious, curious and monstrous creatures…

events.name: Bake something!
events.excerpt: The new special exhibition "Bake Something!" is a fun baking adventure with a mouse and a cat for children ages 4 to 12.

events.name: Computer games. Evolution of a medium
events.excerpt: The first computer game museum in the world was founded in Berlin. An iconic time trip for the whole family through 60 years of history of the games can start.

events.name: DeJa Vu Museum Berlin
events.excerpt: A unique experience with wow moments awaits you at the Museum of Optical Illusions at Alexanderplatz. Celebrate a feast for the senses, take cool photos and marvel at amazing effects.

events.name: Form field to fork
events.excerpt: How many people eat with knife and fork worldwide, how many use fingers and hands? When and where was the can invented – or margarine? How is the typical life of a pig in an industrialized farm vs. a pig in an organic farm?

events.name: Gothic house - Life in the city
events.excerpt: An exhibition on the history of urban life and housing in Spandau on the upper floor of the Gothic House. This exhibition, suitable for the whole family, is part of the Spandau Museum of Local History, which is housed in the Armory at the…

events.name: Kinder-Reich: the Gemäldegalerie for Kids. The Painter's Workshop
events.excerpt: In the new 'Kinder-Reich' at the Gemäldegalerie, children can find out for themselves how Dutch 17th-century paintings were created.

events.name: Mehr Teen Gropius Bau (AT)
events.excerpt: Everyone who is between 15 and 19 years old and interested in art and culture is invited: Develop a program in the Gropius Bau precisely for this age group. What could this program look like? How should your working group function?

events.name: TALENTOPIA - The exhibition to join in
events.excerpt: What's inside you? This question is the focus of the new interactive exhibition TALENTOPIA, which can be experienced at the Labyrinth Kindermuseum Berlin from May 18, 2025.

events.name: The Solar System
events.excerpt: The highlight of this exhibition is the original 283.5-kilogram meteorite from the Arizona Meteor Crater.

events.name: Time travel through the history of espionage
events.excerpt: Who was the first spy? Did you know that drones were used in World War Two? Which secret service had the best codes? What is the difference between a honey-trap and the Romeo method?

events.name: Villa Global
events.excerpt: Berlin is changing and the Villa Global has also changed. Many new people have moved in: The Next Generation.

events.name: Permanent exhibition DDR Museum
events.excerpt: Everything you want to know about the GDR!

events.name: From hand axes to smartphones
events.excerpt: With 2,000 objects from the collection, the Museum of Communication tells over 40,000 years of communication history on 3,000 square meters - from hand axes to smartphones.

events.name: SuperCity 3000
events.excerpt: What will life be like in the city of the future? This is the question explored by the special exhibition “SuperCity 3000. Our City of the Future” at the German Museum of Technology.

events.name: 2000 years of German history
events.excerpt: In just one hour, the Deutschlandmuseum tells 2,000 years of German history through an immersive experience—from the revolt of the Germanic tribes against the Romans in 9 A.D. to the present day.

events.name: Computer games. Evolution of a medium
events.excerpt: At the Computer Games Museum, experience the virtual worlds of today, as well as the games from your own youth and those of your parents and grandparents.

events.name: Visions of possible futures
events.excerpt: Robot humans, green skyscrapers, collaborative economies: There are endless possibilities for thinking about the future.

events.name: Life in the Middle Ages
events.excerpt: More than 800 years ago, there was a medieval settlement on the site of today’s open-air museum. The permanent exhibition tells its story.

events.name: Bébé Symphonique
events.excerpt: With “Bébé Symphonique,” parents can immerse themselves and their babies and toddlers in a vibrant world of colors and shapes.

events.name: Black Light Workshop: Haunting the Puppet Theatre
events.excerpt: Magical activities and tricks under black light.

events.name: BAUBAU
events.excerpt: Initially conceived as a pilot project by Kerstin Brätsch, a freely accessible play space opened in September 2024 in the west wing of the ground floor, then grow over the next several years and expand into the outdoor area.

events.name: Forum or palace? Family guided tour in German
events.excerpt: The Humboldt Forum in Berlin is a new building with baroque façades reminiscent of the former Berlin Palace: Forum or Palace? New or old?

events.name: Workshop: Dreaming Drawing Club
events.excerpt: Welcome to the Dreaming Drawing Club, where dreams become drawings!

events.name: FACK JU GOEHTE – The Musical
events.excerpt: Experience the funniest class ever! Zeki & Chantal live at BlueMax Theater Berlin. Over 100,000 fans, awarded Best Musical. More chaotic, bold & musical than ever. Showing until Oct 31, 2026 – get your tickets now!

events.name: FACK JU GOEHTE – The Musical
events.excerpt: Experience the funniest class ever! Zeki & Chantal live at BlueMax Theater Berlin. Over 100,000 fans, awarded Best Musical. More chaotic, bold & musical than ever. Showing until Oct 31, 2026 – get your tickets now!

events.name: A Journey of Discovery Through the Mongol Empire
events.excerpt: How do you survive on the Mongolian steppe? Why was a city built there 800 years ago? And who exactly was Genghis Khan?

events.name: Family tour: "DINOSAURS!"
events.excerpt: On this guided tour of the special exhibition “DINOSAURS!”, museum visitors aged five and over will learn about dinosaurs from three geological periods, such as the impressive T.

events.name: POP-UP! Your Workshop
events.venue: Haus Bastian – Zentrum für Kulturelle Bildung
events.excerpt: Pull, twist, fold, flip… What crafts, materials, and tools can you discover in the museum? How were things made here?

events.name: Family Tour
events.excerpt: The Berlinische Galerie invites you to join its Family Tour. On this guided tour, you can experience the exhibition ‘Lovis Corinth. Then came Berlin!’ in a fun and interactive way.

events.name: Of ghosts and spirits
events.excerpt: Waldemar, the castle ghost, is back! Fall is spooky season—at least that’s what Waldemar thinks. And that’s why, together with his assistant Astrid Heiland-Vondruska, he’s telling his favorite ghost stories at the castle.

events.name: Ancient picture stories in 3D
events.excerpt: Explore the Pergamon Frieze, which tells of the battle of the Olympian goddesses against the giants. Decipher the dramatic scenes. Pose yourself.

events.name: Power Posters for Berlin
events.excerpt: Creative leisure activities for children: How do you get your messages, wishes and demands across to people in the city and in your local area without going online?

events.name: Spooky wildlife at Berlin Zoo
events.excerpt: As we all know, October is the spookiest month of the year. Even the zoo’s animal residents have a few secrets that are almost eerie.

events.name: Picture-book cinema
events.excerpt: Every Monday at 4.30 pm and every Tuesday (currently ONLY) at 4.30 pm, there is a picture book cinema for children aged 4 and over.

events.name: Autumn break course
events.excerpt: Have you always wanted to learn how to draw a portrait or a self-portrait?

events.name: Our City, Our History!
events.excerpt: Holiday programme for children: On this course, after-school groups explore the permanent exhibition, discover Berlin from different perspectives and tell their own stories about Berlin.

events.name: F(Olha)/Um(Blättern)
events.excerpt: An interactive dance piece about falling leaves, change and new beginnings.

events.name: Triangle meets circle
events.excerpt: Craft workshop as part of the exhibition ‘KUNSTKNALL – Girl Power in Art’.

events.name: Mr. Eichhorn and the First Snow
events.excerpt: About searching, finding, and staying awake. “Winter,” says the goat, “is beautiful. Snowflakes fall from the sky and everything turns white! Mr. Eichhorn has always slept through winter….”

events.name: Spooky Fun: Ghostly Tales – We make up spooky stories
events.excerpt: Story workshop for children aged 7 to 12. Together with author and literary educator Anja Frisch, you’ll invent and create your very own spooky stories.

events.name: Halloween with Paper: Spooky Paper Masks
events.excerpt: At Halloween, paper becomes the starting point for spooky, imaginative and surprising creations. Together, we’ll make little Halloween creations such as ghosts, bats, spider’s webs, pumpkins and other creepy paper figures.

events.name: DIY Hands-On Wednesday: Werewolves of Düsterwald
events.excerpt: Things are set to get exciting at the library this October: who’s the werewolf, who’s a villager – and who can you still trust?

events.name: Pictures in Sound – Bouncy Tones
events.venue: Deutsche Kinemathek - Museum für Film und Fernsehen
events.excerpt: What does a dancing circle sound like? What noises does a bouncing triangle make? And how can you create your very own animated film out of paper?

events.name: The Grusical

events.excerpt: Auf dieser spannenden, publikumswiksamen Theatertour werden Sie von historischen Gestalten in der dunklen Zeit des Herbstes hautnah in die mystischen Sphären von Halloween und Allerheiligen entführt.

events.name: End-of-season celebrations at the Wuhlheide Park Railway

events.name: Wuhlheide – ABSOLUTELY BRILLIANT!
